chapters.title: Come, let us reason
chapters.summary: Isaiah charges Judah with rebellion and empty worship while injustice fills the land. Yet God invites them: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be white as snow.

chapters.title: The mountain of the Lord
chapters.summary: In the last days nations will stream to God's mountain and beat their swords into ploughshares. But first the proud will be humbled.

chapters.title: Judgment on Jerusalem
chapters.summary: God will take away Judah's leaders and supplies because of their defiance, and judge the proud women of Zion.

chapters.title: The Branch of the Lord
chapters.summary: After cleansing, the Branch of the Lord will be beautiful, and God's glory will shelter Zion like a cloud by day and fire by night.

chapters.title: The song of the vineyard
chapters.summary: God planted a vineyard and found only wild grapes. Woe to those who call evil good and good evil.

chapters.title: Here am I, send me
chapters.summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up while seraphim cry Holy, holy, holy. Cleansed by a coal, he answers, "Here am I; send me."

chapters.title: Immanuel
chapters.summary: Isaiah tells frightened King Ahaz to trust God and offers a sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and call his name Immanuel.

chapters.title: God is with us
chapters.summary: Assyria will sweep over the land like a flood. Do not fear what the people fear; the Lord Himself is to be your sanctuary.

chapters.title: Unto us a child is born
chapters.summary: The people in darkness have seen a great light. Unto us a child is born: Wonderful, Counsellor, the mighty God, the Prince of Peace.

chapters.title: Assyria, the rod of God's anger
chapters.summary: Woe to unjust rulers. Assyria is God's tool for judgment but will itself be judged for its pride. A remnant of Israel will return.

chapters.title: A shoot from Jesse
chapters.summary: A shoot will come from the stump of Jesse, filled with the Spirit. The wolf will dwell with the lamb, and the earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord.

chapters.title: A song of salvation
chapters.summary: On that day God's people will sing: God is my salvation, I will trust and not be afraid. With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.

chapters.title: Judgment on Babylon
chapters.summary: The first of the oracles against the nations: the day of the Lord will come on proud Babylon, which will be overthrown.

chapters.title: The fall of the morning star
chapters.summary: Israel will taunt the king of Babylon: how you are fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning, you who wanted to be like the Most High.

chapters.title: Lament for Moab
chapters.summary: Moab is suddenly destroyed, and the prophet weeps for its people.

chapters.title: Moab's refuge
chapters.summary: Moab is urged to shelter refugees. A throne will be established in mercy in the tent of David.

chapters.title: Damascus and Israel
chapters.summary: Damascus and northern Israel will fall because they forgot the God of their salvation.

chapters.title: A message to Cush
chapters.summary: God watches quietly from His dwelling, and the distant people of Cush will bring gifts to Mount Zion.

chapters.title: Egypt judged and healed
chapters.summary: Egypt will be struck and confused, but in the end Egypt and Assyria will worship with Israel: blessed be Egypt my people.

chapters.title: Isaiah goes barefoot
chapters.summary: Isaiah walks barefoot for three years as a sign that Assyria will lead Egypt and Cush away captive.

chapters.title: Watchman, what of the night?
chapters.summary: Visions of Babylon's fall, and a watchman asked how long the night will last.

chapters.title: The valley of vision
chapters.summary: Jerusalem feasts instead of repenting: let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die. The steward Shebna is replaced by Eliakim.

chapters.title: The fall of Tyre
chapters.summary: The great trading city of Tyre will be humbled, and later its wealth will be given to the Lord.

chapters.title: The earth laid waste
chapters.summary: God's judgment will shake the whole earth because people have broken His everlasting covenant, and then He will reign on Mount Zion.

chapters.title: A feast for all peoples
chapters.summary: God will prepare a feast for all peoples, swallow up death forever and wipe away tears from all faces.

chapters.title: Perfect peace
chapters.summary: A song of trust: You will keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is stayed on You. Your dead shall live.

chapters.title: God's vineyard restored
chapters.summary: God will slay Leviathan and care for His vineyard. Israel will take root and fill the world with fruit.

chapters.title: A cornerstone in Zion
chapters.summary: Drunken leaders scoff at God's warnings, but He lays a precious cornerstone in Zion: whoever believes will not be in haste.

chapters.title: Lip service
chapters.summary: This people honor God with their lips but their hearts are far from Him. Yet a day is coming when the deaf will hear and the blind will see.

chapters.title: In returning and rest
chapters.summary: Judah seeks Egypt's help instead of God. In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and confidence shall be your strength. Your ears will hear a word behind you.

chapters.title: Do not trust Egypt
chapters.summary: Woe to those who rely on horses and chariots instead of looking to the Holy One of Israel, who will defend Jerusalem.

chapters.title: A king in righteousness
chapters.summary: A righteous king will reign, and when the Spirit is poured out, the wilderness will become fruitful and justice will bring peace.

chapters.title: The Lord is our king
chapters.summary: The sinners in Zion tremble. The one who walks righteously will see the King in His beauty. The Lord is our judge, lawgiver and king.

chapters.title: Judgment on the nations
chapters.summary: God's anger falls on all nations, and Edom becomes a desolate wilderness.

chapters.title: The desert blossoms
chapters.summary: The wilderness will blossom like a rose. Strengthen weak hands; the blind will see, and the ransomed will return to Zion with singing.

chapters.title: Assyria threatens Jerusalem
chapters.summary: Sennacherib's field commander mocks Hezekiah and the Lord outside Jerusalem's walls, urging the people to surrender.

chapters.title: Hezekiah's prayer answered
chapters.summary: Hezekiah spreads the Assyrian letter before God and prays. God answers through Isaiah, and the angel of the Lord strikes the Assyrian camp.

chapters.title: Hezekiah's illness
chapters.summary: Hezekiah is told he will die, but he prays and God adds fifteen years, making the shadow on the steps go back as a sign.

chapters.title: Envoys from Babylon
chapters.summary: Hezekiah shows his treasures to Babylonian envoys, and Isaiah foretells that everything will one day be carried to Babylon.

chapters.title: Comfort my people
chapters.summary: Comfort ye my people. Prepare the way of the Lord. The grass withers, but God's word stands forever. Those who wait on the Lord shall mount up with wings as eagles.

chapters.title: Fear not, I am with you
chapters.summary: God challenges the nations and their idols, and comforts Israel His servant: fear not, for I am with you; I will uphold you with My right hand.

chapters.title: My servant
chapters.summary: Behold My servant, in whom My soul delights. He will not break a bruised reed and will bring justice and light to the nations.

chapters.title: When you pass through the waters
chapters.summary: God has redeemed Israel and called them by name. When you pass through the waters I will be with you. I am doing a new thing.

chapters.title: The folly of idols
chapters.summary: God will pour His Spirit on Israel's children. Isaiah mocks the man who burns half a log for warmth and bows down to the other half.

chapters.title: Cyrus, God's anointed
chapters.summary: God names Cyrus to free His people. There is no other God; every knee shall bow and every tongue swear to Him.

chapters.title: Idols carried away
chapters.summary: Babylon's gods must be carried, but Israel's God has carried His people from birth and will carry them in old age.

chapters.title: Babylon humbled
chapters.summary: Proud Babylon, who said she would be a queen forever, will sit in the dust.

chapters.title: Refined in affliction
chapters.summary: God has refined Israel in the furnace of affliction for His own name's sake. Go out from Babylon.

chapters.title: A light to the nations
chapters.summary: The servant will be a light to the Gentiles. Zion thinks God has forgotten her, but can a mother forget her child? I have engraved you on My palms.

chapters.title: The servant's obedience
chapters.summary: The servant does not turn back from those who strike him, for the Lord God helps him.

chapters.title: Look to the rock
chapters.summary: Look to Abraham, the rock you were cut from. God's salvation lasts forever, and the redeemed will return to Zion with joy.

chapters.title: How beautiful are the feet
chapters.summary: Awake, Zion. How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news. The suffering servant is introduced.

chapters.title: The suffering servant
chapters.summary: The servant is despised and rejected, a man of sorrows. He was wounded for our transgressions, and by his stripes we are healed.

chapters.title: Enlarge your tent
chapters.summary: Barren Zion will have many children. With everlasting kindness God will have mercy on her; His covenant of peace will not be removed.

chapters.title: Come to the waters
chapters.summary: Everyone who thirsts, come and buy without money. Seek the Lord while He may be found; His thoughts are higher than ours, and His word will not return empty.

chapters.title: A house of prayer for all
chapters.summary: Foreigners and eunuchs who hold fast to God's covenant will be welcomed: My house shall be called a house of prayer for all people.

chapters.title: The high and lofty One
chapters.summary: Idolatry is condemned, but the high and holy God dwells with those who are contrite and humble in spirit.

chapters.title: The fast God chooses
chapters.summary: God rejects fasting that ignores injustice. The fast He wants is to loose chains, feed the hungry and shelter the poor, and then your light will break forth.

chapters.title: Your sins have separated you
chapters.summary: God's arm is not too short to save, but sin has separated the people from Him. The Redeemer will come to Zion.

chapters.title: Arise, shine
chapters.summary: Arise, shine, for your light has come. Nations will come to Zion's light, and the Lord will be her everlasting light.

chapters.title: Good news to the poor
chapters.summary: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me to bring good news to the poor, bind up the brokenhearted and proclaim liberty, giving beauty for ashes.

chapters.title: A new name
chapters.summary: For Zion's sake God will not rest until her righteousness shines. She will be called by a new name, and watchmen will pray without rest.

chapters.title: God's mercy remembered
chapters.summary: God returns from judging Edom. Then the prophet recalls God's mercies of old: in all their affliction He was afflicted.

chapters.title: We are the clay
chapters.summary: Oh that You would rend the heavens and come down. We are all like an unclean thing, yet You are our Father; we are the clay and You the potter.

chapters.title: New heavens and a new earth
chapters.summary: God answers those who did not seek Him and promises new heavens and a new earth, where there will be no weeping and the wolf and lamb will feed together.

chapters.title: Comfort like a mother
chapters.summary: God looks to the humble and contrite. He will comfort Jerusalem like a mother, and all flesh will come to worship before Him.
